editorNote: Andrew Ng's back with a new company and Coursera's money behind it, Apple's quietly turned its phones into a Klarna-backed lease, and OpenAI open-sourced a security tool without telling anyone — Hacker News beat them to the announcement. Underneath the product news, a behavioral study makes an unglamorous but useful point about AI safety: it's competitive pressure, not risk appetite, that pushes teams toward unsafe shortcuts.

stories.headline: Andrew Ng launches LearnVector, an AI tutoring startup, with $100M from Coursera
stories.summary: Coursera is putting $100M into LearnVector, a new company from co-founder Andrew Ng, for roughly a third of it on a fully diluted basis. LearnVector is building agentic AI that plans, adapts to, and sticks with an individual learner rather than answering one-off questions, with first products targeted for early 2027.
stories.whyItMatters: It's a concrete bet from one of AI's most recognizable figures — and from Coursera's balance sheet — that personalized AI tutors, not just chat interfaces, are the next phase of ed-tech.

sourceLinks.title: Coursera Makes $100 Million Strategic Investment in LearnVector, a New AI-Native Learning Company Founded by Andrew Ng

stories.headline: Apple replaces its iPhone Upgrade Program with a Klarna-backed lease called Apple Upgrade
stories.summary: Apple Upgrade now covers iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Watch with monthly lease pricing starting at $17.99, $11.99, $24.99, and $11.99 respectively, and Klarna charges no financing fee on top of retail price. Lease terms run 12-24 months for iPhone/Watch and 24-36 months for iPad/Mac, with the iPhone 16, Watch SE, MacBook Neo, Mac mini, base iPad, and Studio Display excluded.
stories.whyItMatters: It swaps Apple's old device-payment plan for an actual lease across its whole hardware line, changing how millions of buyers finance an upgrade.

sourceLinks.title: Apple Retires iPhone Upgrade Program for Klarna-Backed Leases

stories.headline: OpenAI quietly open-sources its Codex Security CLI — Hacker News found it before OpenAI announced it
stories.summary: OpenAI released Codex Security CLI, a code-vulnerability scanner and TypeScript SDK it had run as a ChatGPT research preview since March, under an Apache-2.0 license with no formal announcement. OpenAI's own acknowledgment came after the fact: "We quietly released the open-source Codex Security CLI, but Hacker News found it before we had a chance to share it here." The tool scans repositories, tracks findings across scans, and plugs into CI, though it can't yet resume an interrupted scan.
stories.whyItMatters: A company that usually stage-manages its launches let this one slip out untouched, handing developers a free, open vulnerability-scanning agent in the process.

sourceLinks.title: The security review AI 'Codex Security CLI' has been open-sourced and is now available for download from GitHub

stories.headline: Study: it's falling behind, not risk appetite, that pushes AI teams toward unsafe development
stories.summary: In a paired behavioral experiment, participants repeatedly chose between a slower 'safe' and faster 'unsafe' development path with capped personal risk; the strongest predictor of choosing unsafe wasn't individual risk tolerance but falling behind an opponent, while being ahead reduced unsafe choices. An accompanying evolutionary-game model found the same dynamic across strategies, leading the authors to argue interventions should target competitive pressure itself, not just individual risk-taking.
stories.whyItMatters: It reframes the AI-race safety debate: slowing any one lab's risk appetite may matter less than reducing the competitive pressure that makes falling behind feel dangerous.

sourceLinks.title: Falling Behind Drives Unsafe Development in an Idealised AI Race Experiment

stories.headline: Kimi K3's architecture notes show a 2.8T-parameter model with no positional embeddings at all
stories.summary: A detailed technical writeup of Kimi K3 — scaled up from the 48B Kimi Linear to 2.8T parameters — describes a LatentMoE layer that compresses large linear layers, a mix of multi-head latent attention and Kimi Delta Attention in place of regular attention, and cross-layer attention-based residual connections that cost about 4% more to train and 2% more to serve in exchange for better validation loss. Most notably, it drops RoPE entirely in favor of no positional embeddings anywhere, which the analysis calls the first frontier-scale model to do so.
stories.whyItMatters: It's a concrete data point in the industry's shift from scaling parameter count to redesigning architecture for inference efficiency, alongside DeepSeek V4 and Nemotron 3.

sourceLinks.title: Kimi K3 Architecture Overview and Notes
